Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Economy | Telecom MTN Group reaffirms long-term investment commitment to Ghana Source : Nanabanyin Brown-Addo 20 November 2026 9:27am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Board Chairman of MTN Group, Mcebisi Jonas, has reaffirmed the telecommunications and fintech giant's commitment to continued investment in Ghana, describing the country as a key market within the Group's operations.
He gave the assurance during a meeting with Ghana’s Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, in Accra on Wednesday, November 18, as part of activities marking MTN Ghana's 30th anniversary.
Mr Jonas, who was accompanied by MTN Ghana Chief Executive Officer, Stephen Blewett, highlighted the company's contribution to economic growth and employment creation, adding that MTN remains committed to creating long-term value for Ghanaians.
He also stressed the importance of collaboration between government and the private sector in advancing Ghana's digital transformation.
"Ghana has been an important part of MTN's story for three decades, and our commitment to its future remains as strong as ever," he said.
He added that the company intends to translate its partnership with government into investments that improve connectivity, expand opportunities and support the country's digital agenda.
Dr Ato Forson welcomed the delegation and commended MTN for its sustained investment in Ghana's telecommunications and digital financial services sectors.
He noted that partnerships between government and the private sector are essential to driving sustainable economic growth and creating jobs.
MTN Ghana began commercial operations in 1996, becoming a pioneer in the introduction of GSM mobile telephony in the country.
Over the past three decades, the company has expanded beyond telecommunications into digital financial services and other areas of the digital economy.
Its contributions include capital investment, tax payments, local shareholding through its listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange, and social interventions through the MTN Ghana Foundation.
The latest engagement with the Finance Ministry forms part of a series of stakeholder meetings marking the company's 30 years of operations.
